questions.stem: Which word is most nearly a synonym for COVET?

guide.explanation: Covet means desire strongly. Admiration, purchase and a request can occur without coveting.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly a synonym for RELUCTANT?

guide.explanation: Reluctant means unwilling or hesitant to act; ability, certainty and preparation are different issues.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly a synonym for CONCISE?

guide.explanation: Concise means expressed in few words. A statement can be precise or blunt while remaining lengthy; incomplete means missing content.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly a synonym for OBSOLETE?

guide.explanation: Obsolete means no longer current or in use; damage, rarity and unpopularity alone do not make something obsolete.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly a synonym for IMPARTIAL?

guide.explanation: Impartial means free of favoritism. A person may be informed and involved yet impartial.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly a synonym for RESILIENT?

guide.explanation: Resilient describes recovery after stress or difficulty, not rigid resistance to all change.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly a synonym for FRUGAL?

guide.explanation: Frugal means avoiding waste. It does not establish poverty, lack of generosity, or lack of ambition.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly a synonym for CANDID?

guide.explanation: Candid means honest and direct; candor does not require rudeness, confidence, or informality.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly a synonym for VIGILANT?

guide.explanation: Vigilant means alert and watchful; fear or suspicion may accompany it but is not its definition.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly a synonym for PLAUSIBLE?

guide.explanation: Plausible means apparently reasonable or believable, without proof or certainty.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly a synonym for COAX?

guide.explanation: To coax is to persuade gently, rather than command or simply give an explanation.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly a synonym for SCRUTINIZE?

guide.explanation: To scrutinize is to inspect closely; it need not involve memorizing or summarizing.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly a synonym for ALLEVIATE?

guide.explanation: Alleviate means make less severe, not necessarily remove, hide, or delay.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly a synonym for REPLENISH?

guide.explanation: Replenish means fill or supply again. Replacing a container or distributing its contents is different.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly a synonym for PROHIBIT?

guide.explanation: Prohibit means disallow. Regulation or discouragement may stop short of a ban.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly a synonym for NIMBLE?

guide.explanation: Nimble means quick and skillful in movement; haste, restlessness or low weight alone is insufficient.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly a synonym for STURDY?

guide.explanation: Sturdy means strongly built. Something can be heavy or rigid without being strong.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly a synonym for TRANQUIL?

guide.explanation: Tranquil means calm and peaceful, not necessarily remote, sleepy, or still.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: As an adjective describing a design, which word is closest in meaning to ELABORATE?

guide.explanation: As an adjective, elaborate means complex or carefully detailed. Cost or decoration alone does not define it.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly a synonym for INERT?

guide.explanation: Inert means inactive or lacking motion; the narrower distractor does not capture the general sense.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly a synonym for TENTATIVE?

guide.explanation: Tentative means not yet final or certain, hence provisional; it need not be unplanned.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly a synonym for REPRIEVE?

guide.explanation: A reprieve is a postponement of punishment or temporary relief; it need not remove blame or give permanent immunity.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly a synonym for CONSPICUOUS?

guide.explanation: Conspicuous means easy to notice; fame, color and unusualness are possible causes rather than definitions.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly a synonym for WARY?

guide.explanation: Wary means alert to possible danger and cautious. Weary concerns tiredness; the other descriptions are too specific.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly a synonym for VERIFY?

guide.explanation: Verify means establish truth or accuracy. Endorsement and repetition do not establish it.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to AUTHENTIC?

guide.explanation: Authentic means genuine; counterfeit means made to pass as genuine. Age, rarity and price are not opposites.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to RIGID?

guide.explanation: Rigid means stiff or resistant to bending; flexible is the opposite. Brittleness concerns breaking.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to DURABLE?

guide.explanation: Durable means able to last or withstand wear; fragile contrasts with that resistance. Replaceability does not imply fragility.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to EXPAND?

guide.explanation: Expand means become larger; shrink means become smaller. The other options describe enlargement.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to CONCEAL?

guide.explanation: Conceal means hide; reveal means make known or visible. Shelter and retain do not oppose hiding.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to OPTIMISTIC?

guide.explanation: Optimistic expects favorable outcomes; pessimistic expects unfavorable ones. Realism or caution is not inherently pessimistic.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to BENEVOLENT?

guide.explanation: Benevolent means wishing good; malicious means intending harm. Indifference lacks the opposite positive intention to harm.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to TRANSPARENT?

guide.explanation: Transparent allows a clear view through; opaque blocks it. Translucent transmits light diffusely and is not the strongest opposite.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to VOLUNTARY?

guide.explanation: Voluntary means freely chosen; compulsory means required. Unpaid or deliberate actions can be voluntary.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to INITIAL?

guide.explanation: Initial concerns the beginning; final concerns the end. Recent concerns how long ago something happened.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to ASCEND?

guide.explanation: Ascend means move upward; descend means move downward. Retreat is backward movement rather than necessarily downward.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to MITIGATE?

guide.explanation: Mitigate means make less severe; worsen means make more severe. Inaction does not itself name that opposite change.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to DILIGENT?

guide.explanation: Diligent means showing steady care; negligent means failing to take proper care. Fatigue or inexperience does not establish negligence.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to INCLUDE?

guide.explanation: Include means have as a part; exclude means keep out. Separating or dividing can leave things included in a larger set.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to HOSTILE?

guide.explanation: Hostile means antagonistic; friendly is the opposite. Neutral and distant lack hostility without expressing friendliness.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to APPROXIMATE?

guide.explanation: Approximate means close but not exact; exact supplies the opposite. Rounded and estimated can be approximate.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to PERILOUS?

guide.explanation: Perilous means dangerous. Familiarity or predictability does not make something safe.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to DORMANT?

guide.explanation: Dormant means inactive, often temporarily; active is the opposite. Slow development is still activity, but is a narrower and less direct choice.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: In a description of speed, which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to ACCELERATE?

guide.explanation: Accelerate means increase speed in this everyday sense; decelerate means reduce it, without requiring an abrupt stop.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to UNANIMOUS?

guide.explanation: Unanimous means fully in agreement; divided contrasts disagreement. Silence or uncertainty does not establish division.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to DOCILE?

guide.explanation: Docile means readily guided or taught; defiant actively resists. Independence alone does not imply defiance.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to REINFORCE?

guide.explanation: Reinforce means make stronger; weaken means make less strong. Replacement or reshaping need not weaken anything.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to LEGIBLE?

guide.explanation: Legible means clear enough to read; unreadable is the opposite in that sense.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to SELDOM?

guide.explanation: Seldom means rarely, so frequently is the opposite. Occasionally is closer to an infrequent rate.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to WANE?

guide.explanation: Wane means decrease in strength or extent; increase reverses that direction. Fluctuation includes both directions.
guide.shortcut: Decide the word’s meaning before checking whether a synonym or an opposite is requested.

questions.stem: Complete the analogy: glossary : unfamiliar terms :: legend : ?

guide.explanation: A glossary explains unfamiliar terms; a map legend explains its symbols. Distances and names can appear on maps without being what the legend primarily defines.
guide.shortcut: State the relationship, then keep the same direction and degree of specificity.

questions.stem: Complete the analogy: thermometer : temperature :: odometer : ?

guide.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature; an odometer measures distance traveled.
guide.shortcut: Describe the first relationship in a short sentence and preserve its direction.

questions.stem: Complete the analogy: bud : blossom :: caterpillar : ?

guide.explanation: A bud develops into a blossom; a caterpillar develops into a butterfly.
guide.shortcut: Describe the first relationship in a short sentence and preserve its direction.

questions.stem: Complete the analogy: editor : manuscript :: mechanic : ?

guide.explanation: An editor works to improve a manuscript; a mechanic works to repair an engine.
guide.shortcut: Describe the first relationship in a short sentence and preserve its direction.

questions.stem: Complete the analogy: stanza : poem :: scene : ?

guide.explanation: A stanza is a structural part of a poem; a scene is a structural part of a play.
guide.shortcut: Describe the first relationship in a short sentence and preserve its direction.

questions.stem: Complete the analogy: insulate : heat loss :: waterproof : ?

guide.explanation: Insulating reduces heat loss; waterproofing prevents water penetration.
guide.shortcut: Describe the first relationship in a short sentence and preserve its direction.

questions.stem: Complete the analogy: murmur : shout :: drizzle : ?

guide.explanation: Murmur and shout contrast low and high intensity of voice; drizzle and downpour contrast light and heavy rain.
guide.shortcut: State the relationship, then keep the same direction and degree of specificity.

questions.stem: Complete the analogy: orchard : fruit :: quarry : ?

guide.explanation: An orchard is a source of fruit; a quarry is a source of stone.
guide.shortcut: Describe the first relationship in a short sentence and preserve its direction.

questions.stem: Complete the analogy: whisper : speak :: stroll : ?

guide.explanation: Whispering is a quiet way of speaking; strolling is a leisurely way of walking.
guide.shortcut: Describe the first relationship in a short sentence and preserve its direction.

questions.stem: Complete the analogy: blueprint : building :: outline : ?

guide.explanation: The first item is a plan for the second: a blueprint plans a building, and an outline plans an essay.
guide.shortcut: State the relationship, then keep the same direction and degree of specificity.

questions.stem: Complete the analogy: fragile : shatter :: flammable : ?

guide.explanation: Something fragile is easily shattered; something flammable is easily ignited.
guide.shortcut: Describe the first relationship in a short sentence and preserve its direction.

questions.stem: Complete the analogy: seed : sow :: evidence : ?

guide.explanation: One sows a seed and presents evidence; preserve object-to-action order.
guide.shortcut: Describe the first relationship in a short sentence and preserve its direction.

questions.stem: Complete the analogy: opaque : light :: soundproof : ?

guide.explanation: An opaque material blocks light; soundproof material blocks sound.
guide.shortcut: Describe the first relationship in a short sentence and preserve its direction.

questions.stem: Complete the analogy: composer : score :: choreographer : ?

guide.explanation: A composer creates a musical score; a choreographer creates a dance.
guide.shortcut: Describe the first relationship in a short sentence and preserve its direction.

questions.stem: Complete the analogy: anecdote : story :: sonnet : ?

guide.explanation: An anecdote is a kind of story; a sonnet is a kind of poem.
guide.shortcut: Describe the first relationship in a short sentence and preserve its direction.

questions.stem: Complete the analogy: approve : approval :: refuse : ?

guide.explanation: Approval and refusal are nouns naming the respective acts; the other options are an adjective or inflected verb forms.
guide.shortcut: State the relationship, then keep the same direction and degree of specificity.

questions.stem: Complete the analogy: compass : direction :: balance scale : ?

guide.explanation: A compass indicates direction; a balance scale compares masses.
guide.shortcut: Describe the first relationship in a short sentence and preserve its direction.

questions.stem: Complete the analogy: telescope : distant :: microscope : ?

guide.explanation: A telescope helps observe distant objects; a microscope helps observe minute, or very small, objects. Nearness alone is not the defining contrast.
guide.shortcut: State the relationship, then keep the same direction and degree of specificity.

questions.stem: Complete the analogy: preface : beginning :: epilogue : ?

guide.explanation: A preface appears at the beginning of a book; an epilogue appears at its end.
guide.shortcut: Describe the first relationship in a short sentence and preserve its direction.

questions.stem: Complete the analogy: hinge : pivot :: axle : ?

guide.explanation: A hinge permits pivoting movement; an axle provides an axis for rotation. Acceleration, balance and sliding are different functions.
guide.shortcut: State the relationship, then keep the same direction and degree of specificity.

questions.stem: Which word is not a unit of length?

guide.explanation: A liter measures volume; the others measure length.
guide.shortcut: Identify the stated category, then test each choice against it.

questions.stem: Which word is not a musical instrument?

guide.explanation: A melody is a sequence of notes, not an instrument.

questions.stem: Which word is not a type of precipitation?

guide.explanation: A breeze is moving air; rain, sleet and hail fall from clouds.

questions.stem: Which word is not a written account of someone's life?

questions.stem: Which word differs from the others in its relation to certainty?

guide.explanation: Conjecture is a proposed explanation without established proof; the others support or establish a claim.
guide.shortcut: Identify the precise shared relationship; do not choose only by how familiar a word feels.

questions.stem: Which word does not describe a lack of sound?

guide.explanation: Clamorous means noisy, whereas the others describe quiet.

questions.stem: Which item differs from the others in the kind of feature it describes?

guide.explanation: Length, width and height are dimensions; symmetry is a relationship between parts of a shape.

questions.stem: Which word differs from the others in how a statement is presented?

guide.explanation: An implication conveys something indirectly; the others name explicit statements.
guide.shortcut: Identify the precise shared relationship; do not choose only by how familiar a word feels.

questions.stem: Which word is not a form of running water?

guide.explanation: A glacier is a mass of ice; the others are flowing bodies of liquid water.
guide.shortcut: Identify the stated category, then test each choice against it.

questions.stem: Which word differs from the others in its relation to an earlier event?

guide.explanation: A forecast concerns what may happen later; the others concern looking back.
guide.shortcut: Identify the precise shared relationship; do not choose only by how familiar a word feels.

questions.stem: Which word differs from the others in its role in an argument?

guide.explanation: Premises, evidence and reasons support an argument; a conclusion is the claim drawn from that support.
guide.shortcut: Identify the precise shared relationship; do not choose only by how familiar a word feels.

questions.stem: Which term differs from the others in its relationship to the whole?

guide.explanation: An appendix is supplementary material; the others name divisions within the main text. The question concerns structural role, not physical attachment.
guide.shortcut: Identify the precise shared relationship; do not choose only by how familiar a word feels.

questions.stem: Which word is not a synonym for praise?

guide.explanation: A rebuke expresses disapproval; the others express admiration.
guide.shortcut: Identify the stated category, then test each choice against it.

questions.stem: Which word differs from the others in the direction of change it expresses?

guide.explanation: Recede means move back or away; the others describe forward or nearer movement.
guide.shortcut: Identify the precise shared relationship; do not choose only by how familiar a word feels.

questions.stem: Which term differs from the others in when it occurs relative to a performance?

guide.explanation: An encore follows a completed performance; the others prepare for or precede a performance.
guide.shortcut: Identify the precise shared relationship; do not choose only by how familiar a word feels.

questions.stem: Four display cases, J, K, L, and M, stand in a row. J is immediately left of K. M is at the right end. L is not next to M. Which case is at the left end?

guide.explanation: M is fourth. J and K must occupy the second and third positions, leaving L first; putting J,K first would leave L beside M.
guide.shortcut: Use only the stated conditions. Check every candidate against all of them.

questions.stem: All members of Group R belong to Group S. No member of Group S belongs to Group T. Which statement must be true?
choices: No member of R belongs to T.
Some member of T belongs to R.
Every person outside T belongs to S.
Every member of S belongs to R.

guide.explanation: R lies entirely within S, and S has no overlap with T, so R and T cannot overlap. Reversals are unsupported.
guide.shortcut: Use only the stated conditions. Check every candidate against all of them.

questions.stem: Some entries are poems. All poems in the collection are unsigned. Which conclusion must follow?
choices: No signed entry is a story.

guide.explanation: At least one entry is a poem and therefore unsigned; nothing identifies all unsigned entries or all stories.
guide.shortcut: Use only the stated conditions. Check every candidate against all of them.

questions.stem: A box contains exactly one token: red, green, or blue. It is not red. If it is green, its label is striped. The label is not striped. What color is the token?

guide.explanation: Not striped rules out green; not red rules out red. The exhaustive third option is blue.
guide.shortcut: Use only the stated conditions. Check every candidate against all of them.

questions.stem: An exhibit opens only if both the lights and the alarm have been tested. The lights were tested, but the alarm was not. If the rule is followed, what follows?
choices: The exhibit opens with fewer visitors.
Testing the lights also tested the alarm.
The lights must be tested again.

guide.explanation: Both tests are necessary. The missing alarm test rules out opening; none of the other claims is stated.
guide.shortcut: Use only the stated conditions. Check every candidate against all of them.

questions.stem: Only sealed envelopes enter the sorting machine. Envelope R entered the machine. What must be true?

guide.explanation: Entry requires sealing; the statement does not require all sealed envelopes to enter.
guide.shortcut: Use only the stated facts. Do not reverse an implication or change some into all.

questions.stem: Only volunteers who complete training may lead a tour. Iris led a tour, and Theo has not completed training. Assuming the rule was followed, which statement must be true?
choices: Iris was the only volunteer who completed training.
Theo may lead a tour if Iris joins him.
Iris completed training, and Theo may not lead a tour.
Every trained volunteer has led a tour.

guide.explanation: Leading a tour requires training, so Iris completed it. Theo lacks the required training and is not permitted to lead. Training alone does not prove anyone has actually led a tour.
guide.shortcut: Use only the stated facts. Do not reverse an implication or change some into all.

questions.stem: Five cards numbered 1 through 5 are arranged in a row. Card 2 is before card 4, card 4 is before card 1, and card 3 is after card 1. Which of these orders could be used?

guide.explanation: The required chain is 2 before 4 before 1 before 3; 5 is unrestricted. Only the first listed candidate respects the full chain.
guide.shortcut: Use only the stated conditions. Check every candidate against all of them.

questions.stem: Exactly two of four lamps, P, Q, R, and S, are on. P is on. If Q is on, R must be on. Which lamp must be off?

guide.explanation: Turning Q on forces R on and would create three lit lamps with P, contradicting exactly two. Either R or S can be the second lamp.
guide.shortcut: Use only the stated conditions. Check every candidate against all of them.

questions.stem: A parcel goes by rail or by road, but not both. Road parcels require a blue label. This parcel has no blue label. What must be true if all rules were followed?

guide.explanation: No blue label rules out road. The exhaustive rail-or-road choice then forces rail; no other label color is specified.
guide.shortcut: Use only the stated conditions. Check every candidate against all of them.

questions.stem: Each of three folders contains either one sheet or two sheets. Together they contain five sheets. How many folders contain two sheets?

guide.explanation: Three single sheets give three. The two additional sheets must go into two different folders because no folder can contain more than two.
guide.shortcut: Use only the stated conditions. Check every candidate against all of them.

questions.stem: Every volunteer who handles animals has completed training. Noel is a volunteer who has not completed training. What must be true?

guide.explanation: Animal handling requires training, so the stated lack of training rules out that role.
guide.shortcut: Use only the stated facts. Do not reverse an implication or change some into all.

questions.stem: Lena is older than Mo but younger than Paz. Rin is younger than Mo. Who must be the oldest of these four?

guide.explanation: The statements give Paz older than Lena older than Mo older than Rin.
guide.shortcut: Use only the stated conditions. Check every candidate against all of them.

questions.stem: Every green card has a triangle. Some cards with triangles also have dots. Which conclusion is justified?
choices: The facts do not establish whether any green card has dots.

guide.explanation: The dotted triangle cards may or may not include green cards. The facts leave that overlap open.
guide.shortcut: Use only the stated conditions. Check every candidate against all of them.

questions.stem: A display uses either three or four panels. Each panel has exactly two hooks. A count finds seven hooks. Which conclusion follows?
choices: The display must have three panels.
The display must have four panels.
At least one stated fact about the display is incorrect.
One panel must have no hooks.

guide.explanation: The stated rules allow six or eight hooks, never seven. They do not identify which statement fails or establish a specific defect.
guide.shortcut: Use only the stated conditions. Check every candidate against all of them.
